title: SIL dashboard grid layout
description: One user-built dashboard grid. Persisted in DCM (D5) as configuration type 'dashboard-layout', target_key = layout_id, category = the plant model name. Element positions are stored in the 12-column 'lg' coordinate space only; narrower breakpoints are derived at render time by react-grid-layout and are never persisted. Version 1.1 adds one optional, chart-only key (`bindings`) so a chart can hold 1..N series per D7; it is additive, so 1.0 documents validate against it unchanged.

layout_version.description: Schema version of this document shape. The dashboard refuses an unknown MAJOR and renders the layout read-only. 1.1 is additive over 1.0 — every 1.0 document still validates here unchanged, because the only new key (`bindings`) is optional. A writer that emits `bindings` declares "1.1".

layout_id.description: Slug. Also the DCM target_key, so DCM's configuration id is sha1(f'dashboard-layout-{layout_id}').

name.description: Human name shown in the layout picker.

description.description: Free text. Empty string when unused; never absent.

model.description: Which plant this layout was authored against. Used to warn (never to block) when the loaded lexicon does not match.

name.description: Copied from the lexicon's model.name at save time. Also written to DCM metadata.category.

lexicon_version.description: Copied from the lexicon's lexicon_version at save time.

elements.description: Unique on `id`. Order is irrelevant; `position` decides placement.

created_at.description: Set by the backend on first save. Null in a client-authored draft.

updated_at.description: Set by the backend on every save.

updated_by.description: Opaque identity string from the portal session, or null.

cols.description: Fixed at 12 for every 1.x document. Element x/w are in this coordinate space at every breakpoint; react-grid-layout reflows for narrower screens.

binding.description: Addresses exactly one lexicon entry. The triple (collection, name, direction) is required because lexicon `signals` is unique on (name, direction), not on name alone — see parameter-contract spec §6.1.

style.description: toggle = two states; segmented = one button per enum member; select = dropdown. Default chosen from the descriptor: bool -> toggle, enum with 2 members -> toggle, 3..6 -> segmented, >6 -> select.

on_value.description: Only for style 'toggle'. Null means: bool -> true, enum -> the second member's value.

off_value.description: Only for style 'toggle'. Null means: bool -> false, enum -> the first member's value.

min.description: Null = use the descriptor's min. A non-null value may only NARROW the descriptor range; the backend rejects a widening on save.

max.description: Null = use the descriptor's max. Narrowing only.

step.description: Null = derived: 1 for int/uint, (max-min)/200 for float.

scale.description: 'log' requires the effective min and max to be strictly positive; needed for wide-dynamic-range coefficients.

show_input.description: Render a numeric entry box beside the slider for exact values.

commit_on.description: When the typed value is published. Never on keystroke.

thresholds.description: Evaluated in order; first match wins. Null = no tinting.

stale_after_ms.description: No sample for this long -> render the last value dimmed with a stale badge.

window_s.description: Visible time span. Clamped at render to the backend's HISTORY_SECONDS.

y_min.description: Null = use the descriptor's min as the axis hint (an output descriptor's min/max is a display hint only; the plant may legitimately exceed it).

y_autoscale.description: True overrides y_min/y_max and fits the visible window.

stroke.description: Null = the theme palette assigns a distinct colour per series. A non-null value is applied to EVERY series of the chart, so leave it null on a multi-binding chart or all traces render in one colour.

id.description: Stable for the life of the element. Unique within the layout.

binding.description: The singular binding. Null = a placed but unbound element. A binding that no longer resolves against the lexicon is NOT rewritten to null; it is kept and rendered in the unbound state so a lexicon regression cannot destroy a layout. On a chart that also carries `bindings`, this MUST mirror `bindings[0]` — see that property.

bindings.description: Added in 1.1 to satisfy D7: a chart takes 1..N series, because overlaying ocv_v against dc_voltage_v is the point of a chart. Permitted on `type: "chart"` only, and optional even there — an absent `bindings` means the element is single-series and `binding` alone decides it, which is exactly the shape of a 1.0 document. When present, the writer MUST keep `binding` equal to `bindings[0]` so a 1.0 reader still sees a valid single-series chart; JSON Schema cannot express that cross-property equality, so it is a writer obligation, not a validated one. An empty array is legal and means a placed but unbound chart, matching `binding: null`.

allOf.$comment: 1.1: `bindings` is chart-only. No `then` branch — a chart is simply unconstrained here; every other type must not carry the key at all.
